inconsistencies: #35713 (replace Boost.Test with an in-tree runner) and #35139 (new thread-safe ASSERT macros in test utils) address the same problem of moving off Boost test macros. Review #35713 first: it settles which framework the assertions live in, and #35139 should be shaped by that decision or folded into it.

#36729 and #36730 both come out of the same chunked-socket reproducer (#36724) and harden different layers of the Python framework against split recv(). Review them as a pair; #36729 (HTTP) is the simpler of the two.
#36437 explicitly unblocks the follow-up orphanage hole fixes in #36506, so it must be reviewed before that work; it is placed first for that reason.
#36786 depends on #36765 (not in this category); the dependency must land first even though #36786 carries the user-visible payoff.
#35442 bundles and depends on #35433 (deprecating the replaceable RPC arguments) and is draft until that lands; do not review it in isolation.

#36074 (scripted-diff adding util/check.h includes across 153 test files) and #36087 (AssertUnreachable plus two linters across hundreds of files) touch overlapping assertion code in test files; whichever is reviewed second will need a rebase, so pick an order deliberately rather than reviewing them in parallel.

#36788, #36794 and #36797 are three slices of tracking issue #36692 (declarative test data construction), and #35994 is the abandoned automated clang-tidy approach to the same goal. Decide #35994's fate first so the manual slices are not re-litigated one by one.
#32554 supersedes the earlier attempt #32457 to swap in a newer static block fixture; if #32457 is still open it should be closed in favour of this one.
#34360 exists to measure PR #27865 and #35827 was used to measure #35531/#34489; their value is tied to those optimizations being reviewed, not standalone.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: a small head of signal fixes and high-risk-path coverage (flaky CI, consensus/p2p/socket fuzz and unit coverage, platform CI gaps), a long P3 middle of fuzz throughput, benchmarks, runner features and framework hardening, and a large P4 tail of mechanical test-code cleanups. Per the category's ordering (signal, then high-risk coverage, then framework capability, then speed, then cleanliness), several cleanup-flavoured PRs that scored high alone were moved below coverage work, and two misleading-test fixes (#36699, #36587) were raised to sit with the other signal fixes.
